meta.title: Telugu Alphabet
meta.subtitle: 52 letters and signs · both directions, as two cards per letter
meta.desc: The Telugu script: 52 notes, in the traditional order — the thirteen vowels (Telugu tells a short e and o from a long ē and ō), the three signs that sit on them (the sunna, the visarga and the pollu), the thirty-three consonants row by row, then ళ, the joined letter క్ష that every primer teaches with the alphabet, and ఱ, an old letter for r still met in older spellings. The first deck of the Telugu collection. Both directions: see a letter and recall its sound, or see a sound and recall the letter, each a card with its own schedule. Each vowel is shown alone and as the sign it becomes after a consonant, written on క (ఆ · కా), since the sign is what a reader meets most. Every note gives the romanisation the level decks use, the sound described in English words, and one word that shows it, with a speaker beside the letter and the word. The sounds are approximations, as every learner's alphabet gives them; where English has no equivalent — the breathy consonants (kh, gh, bh …), the curled-back retroflex letters (ṭ, ḍ, ṇ, ḷ) against the soft dental t and d — the card says what to do with the tongue or the breath instead. Sources: the standard description of modern standard Telugu; the example words' romanisations are English Wiktionary's, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0).

fields.Name: అ
fields.Sound: a · a short "a", like the u of cup; every consonant carries it unless a sign says otherwise, so it has no sign of its own

fields.Name: ఆ
fields.Sound: ā · "a" as in father, long

fields.Name: ఇ
fields.Sound: i · "i" as in bit, short

fields.Name: ఈ
fields.Sound: ī · "ee" as in see, long

fields.Name: ఉ
fields.Sound: u · "u" as in put, short

fields.Name: ఊ
fields.Sound: ū · "oo" as in food, long

fields.Name: ఋ
fields.Sound: r̥ · said "ru" in Telugu; found in words from Sanskrit

fields.Name: ఎ
fields.Sound: e · "e" as in bed, short

fields.Name: ఏ
fields.Sound: ē · like the a of cake, long, but one pure vowel without the glide into "ee"

fields.Name: ఐ
fields.Sound: ai · "ai" as in aisle

fields.Name: ఒ
fields.Sound: o · a short "o", as in the first sound of obey

fields.Name: ఓ
fields.Sound: ō · like the o of go, long, but one pure vowel without the glide into "oo"

fields.Name: ఔ
fields.Sound: au · "ow" as in cow

fields.Name: సున్న
fields.Sound: ṁ · sunna (anusvāra), the small circle: a nasal said as the n or m that suits the next consonant (n before d, m before b), and "m" at the end of a word, as in పుస్తకం pustakam "book"

fields.Name: విసర్గ
fields.Sound: ḥ · visarga, the two small circles: a breath of "h" after the vowel, in a few words from Sanskrit

fields.Name: పొల్లు
fields.Sound: pollu (virāma), the tick above: the consonant has NO vowel after it. Inside a word the second consonant is usually written small beneath the first instead (an "ottu"), as the double k of అక్క

fields.Name: క
fields.Sound: ka · "k" as in skin — no puff of breath after it

fields.Name: ఖ
fields.Sound: kha · "k" with a strong puff of breath, as in kit said firmly; found mostly in words from Sanskrit, Persian and Hindi

fields.Name: గ
fields.Sound: ga · "g" as in go

fields.Name: ఘ
fields.Sound: gha · "g" followed by a breathy h, as in the middle of doghouse

fields.Name: ఙ
fields.Sound: ṅa · "ng" as in sing; rare, and usually written as the sunna instead

fields.Name: చ
fields.Sound: ca · "ch" as in church, with no puff of breath; in many native words before a, o or u it is said "ts", as in cats

fields.Name: ఛ
fields.Sound: cha · "ch" with a strong puff of breath, as in the middle of church-hill

fields.Name: జ
fields.Sound: ja · "j" as in jam; in many native words before a, o or u it is said "dz", as in adze

fields.Name: ఝ
fields.Sound: jha · "j" followed by a breathy h, as in the middle of hedgehog; rare

fields.Name: ఞ
fields.Sound: ña · "ny" as in canyon; met almost only in the joined letter జ్ఞ, said "gny"

fields.Name: ట
fields.Sound: ṭa · a "t" made with the tip of the tongue curled back to the roof of the mouth (retroflex); the nearest English sound is the t of top

fields.Name: ఠ
fields.Sound: ṭha · the curled-back (retroflex) t, with a strong puff of breath

fields.Name: డ
fields.Sound: ḍa · a "d" made with the tongue tip curled back (retroflex); the nearest English sound is the d of dog

fields.Name: ఢ
fields.Sound: ḍha · the curled-back (retroflex) d, followed by a breathy h

fields.Name: ణ
fields.Sound: ṇa · an "n" made with the tongue tip curled back (retroflex); never starts a word

fields.Name: త
fields.Sound: ta · a soft "t" with the tongue against the back of the upper teeth (dental), as in French or Spanish; no puff of breath

fields.Name: థ
fields.Sound: tha · the dental t with a strong puff of breath — not the "th" of thin

fields.Name: ద
fields.Sound: da · a soft "d" with the tongue against the back of the upper teeth (dental) — not the "th" of this

fields.Name: ధ
fields.Sound: dha · the dental d followed by a breathy h

fields.Name: న
fields.Sound: na · "n" as in no

fields.Name: ప
fields.Sound: pa · "p" as in spin — no puff of breath after it

fields.Name: ఫ
fields.Sound: pha · "p" with a strong puff of breath; many speakers say it as "f"

fields.Name: బ
fields.Sound: ba · "b" as in bat

fields.Name: భ
fields.Sound: bha · "b" followed by a breathy h, as in the middle of clubhouse

fields.Name: మ
fields.Sound: ma · "m" as in man

fields.Name: య
fields.Sound: ya · "y" as in yes

fields.Name: ర
fields.Sound: ra · a tapped "r", one flick of the tongue, as in Spanish pero

fields.Name: ల
fields.Sound: la · "l" as in leaf, said with the tongue forward

fields.Name: వ
fields.Sound: va · between "v" and "w": the lower lip only lightly touches the teeth

fields.Name: శ
fields.Sound: śa · "sh" as in ship

fields.Name: ష
fields.Sound: ṣa · a second "sh", written in words from Sanskrit and made with the tongue curled back; most speakers say it just like శ

fields.Name: స
fields.Sound: sa · "s" as in sun

fields.Name: హ
fields.Sound: ha · "h" as in hand

fields.Name: ళ
fields.Sound: ḷa · an "l" made with the tongue tip curled back to the roof of the mouth (retroflex); never starts a word

fields.Name: క్ష
fields.Sound: kṣa · a joined letter, క్ + ష, said "ksh"

fields.Name: ఱ
fields.Sound: ṟa · the old letter for a second r, in older spellings only; it is said, and now written, as ర (నోఱు is నోరు, "mouth")
